PullRequest.Title: chat: add customization migration assessment telemetry
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

Customization migration assessment telemetry with explicit lifecycle-owned reporting.

- keep computation and hint generation free of telemetry side effects
- expose an explicit `reportMigrationTelemetry(...)` method with aggregate-only payloads
- report completed assessments from the four intended lifecycle surfaces:
  - new chat in the editor
  - new-session composer in the Agents Window
  - existing session open
  - persisted session restore
- emit one event per non-empty migration category with only trigger, category, warning severity, and count
- remove informational severity until it has distinct product semantics
- add lifecycle-owner tests for all four reporting surfaces

Refs #332990

## Validation

- `npm run transpile-client`
- targeted ESLint for changed files
- focused browser tests:
  - `ChatEditor` editor new-chat lifecycle
  - `NewChatWidget` Agents new-session lifecycle
  - `SessionsService` session-open lifecycle
  - `SessionsService` session-restore lifecycle
  - `CustomizationMigrationService` aggregate payload and telemetry-free compute/hint behavior
- changed files have no TypeScript diagnostics
- full type/layer checks remain locally blocked by unavailable Electron modules and the private Claude SDK package restore

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call site, widespread `openChat` tab-navigation callers, session-scoped computation, IPC provider implementation, and zero-ref scope disposal are directly traced. Exact milliseconds vary with installed MCP/customization count, but the repeated mechanism is deterministic.
Findings.PerformanceResource: MCP compatibility resolution, provider source-folder calls, and associated IPC/allocations
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The full assessment repeats once for every `openChat` invocation, so cost grows with chat-tab switches/reopens inside the same session and with the number of MCP servers and customization types.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated background CPU/IPC work and contention while navigating chats
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Switching or reopening child chats only activated the target chat and updated visibility state; it did not recompute customization migrations or MCP support.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Every `openChat` now starts `computeMigrations` for the owning session, even when the session is already active and only its selected child chat changes.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The added call at line 789 invokes `_reportCustomizationMigrationTelemetry` from `_openChat` after every chat load; before this diff `_openChat` performed no migration assessment.
Findings.Title: Gate migration assessment to session changes, not chat-tab opens
Findings.Impact: For sessions with multiple chats, normal tab switching or reopening a side chat repeatedly recomputes the same session-wide assessment. Users with many MCP servers/customizations can see avoidable background CPU and extension-host traffic competing with chat navigation.
Findings.Evidence: `openChat` is the tab-navigation API used throughout `chatGroupsView.ts` and the sessions list, including reopening a closed side chat. The added call reaches `computeMigrations`, which invokes three file-migration computations plus MCP migration. Each file migration calls `provideSourceFolders` for its candidate types (an extension-contributed provider crosses the main-thread/ext-host IPC boundary), and MCP migration acquires a support scope whose initial update waits 50 ms then resolves every known MCP server and local installed-server state. The migration method disposes the scope after each run; refcount zero removes it from `AgentHostActiveClientService`, so a later tab switch reconstructs and reruns that assessment rather than hitting a warm scope.
Findings.Recommendation: Trigger the assessment only when navigation actually changes the active session (for example, compare the previously active session before `_activate`), while keeping the session-open telemetry path for genuine session opens; do not run it for child-chat selection within the same session.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The unbounded fire-and-forget loop, persisted-cardinality source, IPC boundary, and per-root MCP scope key are explicit. The number of pinned sessions and installed MCP servers determines magnitude, not whether the burst occurs.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Concurrent MCP configuration assessments, extension-host IPC calls, promises, and temporary result objects
Findings.PerformanceScaling: Restore launches one four-category assessment per persisted visible session with no limiter; work grows as O(N) assessments and their provider/MCP fan-out, where N is the persisted grid size (which can grow through sticky sessions).
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: A burst of CPU, IPC, and allocation pressure immediately after window restore
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Persisted-session restore resolved sessions and rebuilt the visible grid, with no migration assessment fan-out after layout.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: After `restoreGrid`, all resolved sessions simultaneously start `computeMigrations`; late sessions do the same from `place`, with no queue or concurrency bound.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: The newly added loop at lines 1611-1615 fire-and-forgets `_reportCustomizationMigrationTelemetry` for every already-resolved restored session; before this diff restore rebuilt the grid without launching this assessment work.
Findings.Title: Bound migration assessment concurrency during session restore
Findings.Impact: Restoring a window with several pinned sessions, especially across different workspaces, can produce an avoidable startup CPU/IPC spike and GC pressure while the restored UI is becoming interactive.
Findings.Evidence: `_getVisibleSessionStates` returns every persisted grid slot, and sticky sessions can be appended without a fixed cap. For each restored session, `computeMigrations` starts three file categories and MCP assessment in parallel. File categories call `provideSourceFolders` per effective prompt type (extension providers use main-thread/ext-host IPC), while distinct workspace roots create distinct `AgentHostMcpServerSupportScope`s that each debounce and resolve all MCP server configurations. Because the loop does not await or limit these promises, sessions with different roots execute these assessments concurrently during restore; prompt-list caching does not coalesce the provider-folder or per-root MCP work.
Findings.Recommendation: Feed restore telemetry assessments through a small concurrency limiter or idle queue with restore-token cancellation; coalesce only assessments proven to share the same session/resource key, while still emitting the required per-session aggregate telemetry.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open a new chat in the editor
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The editor first resolves and binds the chat model; the added assessment is started with `void` afterward, so it is off the direct editor-open critical path but can contend with the newly interactive editor.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Discover prompt, instruction, agent, and skill files from configured/user/workspace locations on a cold prompt cache.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one coalesced discovery per effective prompt type while the cache is warm; invalidation makes the next assessment cold.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Opening an empty chat editor did not invoke migration discovery; discovery occurred only when an existing consumer such as first-request hint generation requested it.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the editor-open critical path because the assessment is fire-and-forget, but runs immediately after model binding.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve writable customization source folders through an extension-contributed item provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to the candidate prompt types across three file categories; agent/instruction types may be requested in more than one category.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No source-folder provider calls were initiated by editor open.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off direct editor-open progress, but contributes background IPC/CPU contention.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve compatibility/configuration for all known and installed MCP servers in a per-roots support scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One scope assessment for the session's normalized root set, iterating all known MCP servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Editor open did not acquire an MCP support-assessment scope.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off direct editor-open progress; it starts after a 50 ms debounce and can overlap user interaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit one aggregate telemetry event per non-empty migration category.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero to four telemetry events per assessment.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No migration-assessment telemetry was emitted from this lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: After assessment completion and off editor-open progress.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One assessment per empty-model `setInput`; cost scales with discovered customization types/files and known MCP servers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One `computeMigrations` runs four migration categories via `Promise.all`. Prompt-list reads for the same type coalesce through `IPromptsService` caches, while source-folder resolution and the MCP assessment remain asynchronous; cancellation follows the editor input token except the MCP computation itself does not consume that token.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Cold prompt discovery scans configured/user/workspace sources and then remains cached under file-location watchers; warm assessments reuse those lists. Provider source folders are recomputed, and an MCP support scope is removed when its sole assessment reference is disposed, so later assessments can be cold again.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed call and full compute path are explicit.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact cost depends on cache warmth and the user's MCP/customization inventory; the new assessment path is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: No separate finding for this intended one-shot lifecycle hook; its work is fire-and-forget and normally occurs once per new editor input.

Scenarios.Scenario: Render or change the Agents Window new-session composer draft
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Rendering registers an autorun that immediately fire-and-forgets the assessment when a draft session exists. Composer rendering does not await it, but assessment work overlaps foreground interaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cold prompt-file discovery across user/workspace/configured locations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached discovery per prompt type, shared across concurrent assessments while valid.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Composer rendering and draft replacement did not assess migrations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited by render, but starts immediately from the autorun.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Call extension-host customization providers for source-folder locations.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Several calls per effective candidate type per draft assessment; no result cache in the migration service.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No source-folder IPC was caused by the composer lifecycle.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the render critical path but may overlap picker interaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Assess all known MCP server configurations for the draft's working-directory roots.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One assessment per distinct simultaneous session-type/root key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No MCP compatibility assessment was started by composer draft changes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background work after a 50 ms debounce.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero to four events per completed draft assessment.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One run per distinct observable draft session/resource produced while selecting workspace or agent-host targets; each run scales with customization candidates and MCP servers.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Each run fans into four parallel categories. This hook supplies no cancellation token, so assessments for rapidly replaced drafts can overlap; identical in-flight MCP root keys share a refcounted scope, while distinct root sets do not.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt lists are warm after first discovery; source-folder results are not cached by this service. MCP scopes coalesce only while simultaneously referenced and are removed at refcount zero.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the uncancelled autorun and assessment path; moderate magnitude because typical selection frequency is small.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Users usually make few draft-target changes, so overlap magnitude is uncertain.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding: overlap is possible, but realistic frequency is not strong enough for a separate high-confidence regression beyond the reported hotter paths.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or switch chats in an existing Agents Window session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Session/chat loading completes before the new assessment is fire-and-forget. It does not extend the awaited open promise but runs while the selected chat becomes interactive.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve source folders through extension-host customization providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Several provider calls per `openChat`, based on effective migration candidate types.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Chat-tab navigation did not invoke provider source-folder resolution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the awaited open path but competes with chat interaction.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Rebuild and resolve per-roots MCP compatibility state across known servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per completed assessment after the previous scope reaches zero references; iterates all effective MCP servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Switching chats did not acquire or rebuild this support scope.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero to four events for every completed chat open, including same-session tab switches.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No migration telemetry was emitted by `openChat`.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Every `openChat` call, including child-tab switches and closed-chat reopens in the same session; work scales with navigation frequency, customization candidate types, and MCP server count.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A newer navigation cancels the prior open token, coalescing some prompt calls; MCP assessment ignores that token and completes. Simultaneous same-root MCP consumers share a scope, but each completed run releases and removes the scope, so spaced navigation reruns it.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt lists remain cached between switches. Source-folder provider calls repeat. The MCP support scope has only in-flight/refcount reuse and no warm lifetime after the telemetry assessment releases it.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: `openChat` callers include tab switching/reopening, and the changed call unconditionally starts session-wide assessment after load.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact contention varies with tab-switch frequency and MCP inventory.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported as repeated work because same-session child-chat navigation recomputes session-wide migration state.

Scenarios.Scenario: Restore persisted visible Agents Window sessions
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Grid resolution/layout is awaited first; immediately after `restoreGrid`, assessments are launched without awaiting them. They are off restore completion but overlap the window's post-restore interactive period.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve session-specific source folders through extension-host providers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: O(N × candidate prompt types) calls for N restored sessions, reduced only when a session has no candidates/provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Restore made no migration-provider IPC calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Not awaited by restore, but all calls are injected into the post-restore period.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Assess MCP compatibility/configuration for restored session root sets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one concurrent scope per distinct normalized session-type/root key, each iterating all known MCP servers.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Restore did not create MCP support-assessment scopes.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background startup CPU/allocation work overlapping interactivity.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Submit aggregate migration telemetry per restored session/category.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to 4N events for N restored sessions with all categories non-empty.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Restore emitted no migration assessment telemetry.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off restore completion but contributes to the same burst.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: All persisted visible grid sessions, including an unbounded set of sticky sessions; effective work is one assessment per resolved session and one per late-arriving session.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The added loop fire-and-forgets every assessment with no limiter. Each assessment internally starts four categories in parallel. Same root keys may share an in-flight MCP scope, while distinct workspace roots create independent scopes; extension-provider calls are not restore-batched.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Prompt-list caches amortize filesystem discovery across sessions. Source-folder results remain per-session calls. MCP work coalesces only for identical simultaneously active keys and is otherwise per distinct roots.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: persistence includes all visible grid slots and the changed loop has no await, queue, or limiter.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical persisted grid size is user-dependent, but sticky sessions have no fixed cap and multi-workspace restores are supported.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reported as an unbounded restore-time concurrency burst.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 11 changed files. Two diff-introduced regressions were submitted: repeated full assessments on same-session chat-tab navigation, and unbounded assessment fan-out for persisted-session restore. One-shot editor/composer telemetry hooks were traced but did not independently meet the reporting threshold.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
